blocks.text: Bain Capital Griffin Aircraft Fund | Coverage: aviation / aircraft leasing / lessors    |    Market data to 13 Oct 2026, fund data to 30 Jun 2026

Verdict: BCGAF's baseline quarter reads well: 36.0% of commitments called with the portfolio at 36% of the US$3,750M scaled target, investment-level gross performance of >50% IRR / 1.60x MoM, and realisations printing at 1.40–2.95x gross MoM (all per the GP's Q2'26 update). The caveat is market-side: JPM judges the post-COVID supply-demand imbalance to be normalising, and IBA (via JPM) records the cycle's first mid-life narrowbody value declines — exactly the A320ceo / 737NG metal where the Fund's two portfolio acquisitions concentrate. Holding assessed as "performing, continued monitoring required": no action needed; track the GP's monetisation prints and supply language against the Section 4 trigger lines.

items: Capital call and second ABS series: the Q1-acquired aircraft portfolio was funded at Q2 quarter-end, taking called capital to 36.0% of commitments (ITD contributions US$127.1M, GP); the aircraft then went into the platform's second Master Trust ABS series — US$568M, completed June, spreads tightening versus the inaugural per Ishka (26-Jun-26), exact level not yet disclosed.

Realisation prints are the strongest early signal: the ex-Spirit A320-family aircraft closed Aug-26 (post Q-end) at >50% gross IRR / 2.11x gross MoM; the United 737-9 JOLCO closed at 1.40x (IRR NM on a sub-one-year hold); three further assets pending at est. 1.82–2.95x; US$12.7M distributed post Q-end (all GP, gross pre-fee).
Final close approaching: US$353.0M committed (GP ~US$50M) toward the US$1bn target; final close expected October 2026, with the GP actively evaluating new investments (GP).

IATA halved 2026 industry profit: US$23bn / 2.0% net margin vs the US$41bn / 3.9% forecast of Dec-25, on jet fuel assumed at US$152/bbl (2025: US$90/bbl) — yet load factor is still a record 84.0%E: a cost shock to airline P&Ls, not a demand shock to aircraft (IATA).

First fuel-shock casualties; upgrade cycle closed: Spirit's liquidation and Air Baltic's fleet restructuring return aircraft to the market while removing weak lessee credits (JPM); Moody's upgraded Avolon to Baa2, effectively ending the lessor upgrade cycle (JPM).

Left: passenger demand by region, May-26 (latest complete IATA set) — five of six regions positive; the Middle East (−28.4%) is the contained drag, narrowing through July per Barclays. Right: industry net profit vs load factor (IATA) — a record 84.0% load factor against profits halved to US$23bn frames 2026 as a cost shock, not a demand shock.

items: Vintage concentration is the live risk: deployment is fastest exactly where values turned — 36.0% called at age ~1 vs Castlelake Aviation V Stable Yield's 28.3% at age ~3 (PitchBook) — and the two portfolio acquisitions (46% of portfolio value: PA#2 40% + PA#1 6%, GP) are weighted to the A320ceo / 737NG vintages where IBA records the first declines. Mitigants: 5–10% purchase-price discounts (GP scorecard: meeting), staged VietJet 737-8 deliveries through 2H26, and simultaneous selling into the same bid at 1.40–2.95x — a two-sided book, not a one-way ramp.

Lease-income insulation is contractual, not economic: it holds until a lessee files, as Spirit and Air Baltic have just demonstrated. The watch-list is the Tier-3 tail (~40% of exposure by credit tier, Junson pixel-read of the GP chart) and fuel-exposed European short-haul, where Barclays' August screen-scrape shows achieved intra-Europe fares down at every full-service carrier tracked.

Funding is the platform's measurable edge: the inaugural Master Trust (Nov-25, US$1,245M) was the largest aircraft ABS ever issued, with a 77.6% senior LTV at single-A (Fitch presale) vs 69–75% at discrete-trust peers; series 2 (Jun-26, US$568M) carries the Fund's aircraft and priced tighter per Ishka. The same spread compression that funds the GP's pipeline is compressing new-delivery lease rate factors on the asset side.

blocks.html: 4. Our Position: Assessment, Watch List & Action
blocks.text: 4. Our Position: Assessment, Watch List & Action

items: Overall assessment: performing, monitoring required. Deployment, realisations and funding all run ahead of plan on the GP's Q2 numbers (nine of eleven scorecard parameters meeting target), and fund-level metrics stay NM until >50% called — so the realisation prints (2.11x ex-Spirit, 1.40x United JOLCO) are the strongest early signal. The quarter's key tension is narrative: the GP's letter leans on record backlog and scarcity while JPM judges the imbalance “is or will normalise” — the pace and pricing of the five in-progress monetisations is the practical test.

blocks.text: Action: continue to hold; no change. The baseline quarter shows deployment, realisation and funding metrics all ahead of plan per the GP, while the market section marks where the cycle is turning — first mid-life narrowbody value declines, normalising supply. Track the watch list quarterly; take the position back to IC only if monetisation prints disappoint or the GP's supply language turns.
